base: black-and-white editorial vintage documentary photograph, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film texture. WIDE HORIZONTAL LANDSCAPE orientation, 3:2 aspect ratio, much wider than tall. FRAMING IS CRITICAL: the camera is CLOSE and the subject is VERY LARGE, filling the entire BOTTOM THREE QUARTERS of the frame from the left edge to the right edge, extending past the bottom edge. Only a NARROW BAND across the very TOP of the frame, about one fifth of the height, is empty pale bright almost-white wall or light, completely free of objects. EVERYTHING IS IN SHARP CRISP FOCUS, deep depth of field, no blur, no bokeh, no soft focus. This is ONE single real photographic exposure, never a composite: every element shares the same light and grain. THE TOP OF THE FRAME IS BRIGHT OVEREXPOSED LIGHT, and the transition from the scene into that light is GRADUAL and soft, as if the light swallows the upper part of the scene: NO horizontal edge anywhere, no shelf edge, no ceiling line, no sign, no roofline crossing the top. Surfaces and objects fade softly upward into the light. THE TOP BAND IS A HARD REQUIREMENT: that top fifth must be ONE single continuous evenly-lit pale surface spanning the FULL width, bright and uniform, with NOTHING crossing it at all: no shelf, no beam, no lamp, no head, no edge of any object. It must read as smooth blank paper. NO fog, NO mist, NO haze and NO smoke anywhere inside the scene itself; only that narrow band at the very top is pale. Natural unposed body language. Brazil, 1960s to 1970s; every sign, card, notebook, photograph, uniform or object in the scene is PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no printed brand names, no logos, no legible writing of any kind; any papers, notebooks, punch cards or photographs show only vague illegible marks, never readable letters or numbers. No text, no words, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no emojis, no gradients, no added color, no stock photo look.
cinema: CINEMATIC DIRECTION: camera at chest height, one strong directional light source raking across the scene, deep shadows, dramatic contrast. People LARGE and CLOSE, chest up, heads at about one fifth from the top of the frame. Every person is FULLY inside the frame: heads complete with clear empty space above them, nobody cropped at the neck, shoulders or waist, nobody touching the left or right edges.
fit: COMPOSITION FOR THE SLIDE (HARD REQUIREMENT): the subject occupies ONLY the LOWER 55 percent of the frame; the ENTIRE UPPER 45 percent of the frame is a plain, flat, evenly lit surface in a very pale OFF-WHITE tone (like unbleached linen paper, hex F3F3F3), with a faint fine texture and absolutely nothing on it: no shelves, no objects, no doorway, no window, no sign, no ceiling line, no heads. That pale surface is part of the photograph and simply continues upward, staying very pale and uniform to the top edge.

images.scene: Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a small neighborhood pharmacy: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties wearing a plain white coat, standing behind his wooden counter and SHRUGGING, both shoulders raised, both palms turned up and open, eyebrows lifted, the resigned 'what can I do about it' gesture; the counter in front of him is bare and empty. LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Street level view of ONE continuous plain plastered facade holding two small adjacent shops, no signs, no lettering: the LEFT shop closed, its corrugated metal roll-down shutter pulled all the way down to the pavement; the RIGHT shop open, its doorway lit from inside, a single customer seen from behind stepping in through the door. The tops of both shutter frames end in the lower half of the frame; the plain pale facade wall continues above them, empty.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a beverage distributor warehouse: the owner, a heavy Brazilian man in his fifties in a sweaty short-sleeved shirt, standing between stacks of plain wooden bottle crates, scribbling a price with a pencil stub on a torn scrap of cardboard held flat against his own palm, another pencil behind his ear, improvising; crates only in the lower part of the frame. LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a small workshop-factory: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties in a short-sleeved shirt, leaning on a wooden counter and complaining to a visiting friend beside him, pointing his THUMB back over his own shoulder toward a young employee working at a bench farther back, seen from behind, head down; the two men in front are LARGE and close, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Still life, NO PEOPLE, inside a small paint store: a long wooden shelf SAGGING badly under the weight of plain unlabeled metal paint cans, propped up from below by a broomstick wedged under it and a piece of rope tied from the shelf to a nail in the wall, the improvised repair; the shelf sits low in the frame; the bare pale plaster wall continuing above it, empty.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Still life, NO PEOPLE, on a worn wooden desk in a cramped back office: an old cardboard shoebox OVERFLOWING with crumpled receipts, folded slips and loose papers spilling over the sides onto the desk, a pencil stub beside it, no ledger, no notebook; all papers plain with only vague illegible gray marks; the desk low in the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a small glass and mirror shop: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties, shirt sleeves rolled up, standing still in front of a large plain mirror leaning against the wall, staring at his own reflection with a serious, sober face; both the man and his reflection LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a small print shop: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties, at the head of a plain wooden table with three employees in work aprons seated around it, a notebook open on the table showing only vague illegible marks, the owner pointing at one line with his index finger, the three employees all looking at the notebook; everyone LARGE, chest up, heads in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside an empty small shop with bare floor: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties, crouching in PROFILE and lifting the corner of a worn old rug with one hand, revealing underneath it rotten, cracked, broken wooden floorboards with a dark hole; he is looking down at the hole; his whole figure in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a beverage distributor warehouse in daylight: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties in a short-sleeved shirt, walking slowly between stacks of plain wooden bottle crates holding a clipboard, counting the crates and writing on the sheet (only vague illegible marks), concentrated; LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above.

Brazil, 1960s to 1970s. Inside a small print shop: the owner, a Brazilian man in his fifties in a work apron over a shirt with rolled sleeves, standing in the middle of the room in front of an old printing press, arms crossed, looking straight into the camera with a calm, firm face; the press and a low shelf only in the lower part of the frame; NO doorway, NO door frame, NO vertical post anywhere; LARGE, chest up, head in the lower half of the frame; the bare pale wall continuing above and spanning the full width.
